blogs.title: Beyond Tokens: Why the Next Generation of LLMs Might Forget Tokenizers Entirely
blogs.description: Current LLMs rely on 'tokenization'—a pre-processing step that groups bytes into chunks. While efficient, this creates biases, struggles with noise, and treats different languages unequally. This post explains how the Byte Latent Transformer (BLT) breaks free from fixed vocabularies by processing raw bytes directly, offering a more robust and linguistically fair foundation for AI.

blogs.title: Smart Scaling: How 'Entropy Patching' Gives LLMs a Human-Like Brain
blogs.description: Why should an AI use the same amount of 'brain power' to predict the letter 's' at the end of a word as it does to start a new sentence? This post explores BLT's 'Entropy Patching' mechanism, which dynamically allocates more compute to complex, high-uncertainty data while skipping the heavy lifting for predictable patterns, making inference significantly more efficient.

blogs.title: The Scaling Hack: How BLT Lets You Build Bigger Models for the Same Cost
blogs.description: In the world of AI, there is usually a trade-off between model size and inference speed. This post breaks down the paper's groundbreaking finding: by using 'patches' instead of tokens, BLT allows developers to simultaneously increase model size and patch size. This unlocks a new way to scale models while keeping inference costs under control.

blogs.title: Spelling Bees and Typos: Why Byte-Level Models are More Robust
blogs.description: Token-based models often stumble when faced with typos, weird spellings, or obscure languages because those specific 'tokens' weren't in their training set. This post highlights how BLT’s byte-level approach gives it a 'superpower' for character-level understanding, making it much better at handling noisy data, phonology, and low-resource languages.

blogs.title: Giving Llama a Byte-Level Upgrade: The 'Byte-ifying' Workflow
blogs.description: You don't always have to start from scratch. This post explains the researchers' fascinating method for 'byte-ifying' existing models like Llama 3. By initializing a Byte Latent Transformer with the weights of a pre-trained token-based model, we can potentially inherit massive amounts of knowledge while gaining the robustness of a byte-level architecture.
